methodology: Official Frontex procurement pages used to confirm Funding & Tenders authority identifier 47352434 and procurement publication channels
Official EU Funding & Tenders public Search API for Frontex open, forthcoming/planned and closed procurement, including low/middle-value procedures
Official TED Search API for formal Frontex notices and contract-award data from 2020-present using Frontex-specific buyer names

Official Frontex Copernicus programme page used to define operational relevance: Copernicus Border Surveillance Service, optical/radar satellites, EUROSUR Fusion Services and external EO suppliers

Calibrated classifier separating core space/EO from generic aviation/drones while retaining Frontex-specific GEOINT/IMINT, contextual EUROSUR and HAPS near-space procurement as dual-use space-security intelligence
limitations: Annual Procurement Plans are planning documents and may be amended; the collector parses both base plans and amendments when linked by Frontex.

Generic drones, aircraft, aerostats, radar and border-surveillance equipment is not automatically classified as space; GEOINT/IMINT, contextual EUROSUR, satellite-RF detection and HAPS near-space surveillance are treated as relevant dual-use space-security procurement.
Research grants, prize contests, Requests for Information and innovation studies are not treated as procurement unless they appear in the formal procurement sources.
TED notice history is grouped by procedure reference before semantic use; raw notices are retained separately for audit.

The local pdf-parse library can fail to preserve Frontex procurement-plan table tokens. V1.5 therefore uses a minimal verified fallback for two official plan entries (HAPS 2026 and GIS/GEOINT/IMINT 2025); historical-plan rows are not counted as currently planned opportunities.

methodology: Official EUROCONTROL public procurement catalogue, including Current business opportunities, Awarded contracts and Upcoming business opportunities

Public catalogue pagination is unioned across multiple official sort orders (Most recent, A-Z, Z-A, Relevance) to recover pagination inconsistencies and continues until the advertised awarded total is reached where possible
Targeted catalogue searches for GNSS, Galileo, EGNOS, ARAIM, satellite, space weather and SATCOM supplement the paginated catalogue so relevant records are not lost if catalogue pagination shifts

Relevant procurement PDFs are downloaded and parsed to enrich classification where the catalogue title alone is insufficient; a previously confirmed core-space title cannot be demoted merely because the PDF also contains generic administrative words

Conservative classifier focused on GNSS/Galileo/EGNOS/PNT, ARAIM/SBAS, satellite communications, space weather, space-based surveillance, RF/interference monitoring and tightly contextualized CNS/datalink/U-space procurement
limitations: EUROCONTROL is an intergovernmental organisation and follows its own Contract Regulations; it is not an EU agency and its procurement is not expected to be complete in TED or the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
Supplier names are only captured if exposed in the public catalogue or procurement documents; secure supplier-portal information is not scraped.
Generic ATM software, facilities, training and corporate procurement is excluded from the primary space RAG.
Datalink, surveillance, spectrum and U-space procurement without explicit satellite/GNSS or multiple space-enabled ATM signals is kept for manual review rather than automatically classified as space.

methodology: ESO In-Tend public portal for current, forthcoming and awarded procurement since November 2022

Official ESO legacy procurement tables for historical calls and price inquiries around the 2020-2022 transition; the >=150 kEUR page is parsed with its native Cft No/Date/Division/Subject/Details structure and preserves later award/status updates

Conservative European space-industry classifier focused on telescope/instrument systems, optics, adaptive optics, detectors, cryogenics, RF/receivers, precision mechanics, scientific software/data and observatory engineering
limitations: The ESO In-Tend portal is JavaScript-heavy and can present reCAPTCHA/anti-bot challenges. If the local run returns zero In-Tend rows, this does NOT mean ESO has zero current/forthcoming/awarded procurements; it means the live layer is not machine-readable through plain HTTP from this collector.

ESO is an intergovernmental astronomy organisation, not an EU agency. The RAG scope therefore means procurement relevant to the European space/astronomy industrial supply chain, not EU public procurement in the narrow legal sense.
Generic catering, office, travel, HR and non-technical facilities procurement is excluded.
Supplier/award details depend on what the public In-Tend pages expose without authentication.
